title: Select letters of Christopher Columbus : $b With other original documents relating to his four voyages to the New World
subjects: America -- Discovery and exploration -- Spanish -- Early works to 1800
summary: "Select letters of Christopher Columbus" by Christopher Columbus is a collection of historical letters written in the late 15th and early 16th centuries. Presented in translation with supporting editorial material, it gathers firsthand accounts of his four voyages to the New World alongside related contemporary documents, illuminating routes, encounters, and the hardships of exploration. The opening of this volume begins with a transcriber’s note and an editor’s preface in which R. H. Major defends his earlier work and the Hakluyt Society against J. A. Froude’s public criticisms. It then launches into a broad introduction surveying real and supposed pre-Columbian discoveries—from classical hints and the Atlantis legend to Chinese, Norse, Arab, Welsh, Venetian (Zeno), Portuguese, and Danish claims—before affirming Columbus’s singular achievement in vision, method, and impact. The introduction proceeds to sketch his background and studies, influences such as Toscanelli and Pierre d’Ailly, his years in Portugal and marriage at Porto Santo, the failed appeal to King John II and departure for Spain, the support won at La Rábida and at court amid theological scrutiny in Salamanca, and the delays preceding the 1492 voyage. It closes this opening stretch by noting debates over his first landfall in the Bahamas and weighing competing identifications proposed by later scholars and navigators.
